rich_summary: Saunaka asks what the mighty serpents did after hearing their mother’s curse. Sauti narrates the story of Sesha, the noblest among them. Disturbed by the cruelty, jealousy, and hostility of his brothers—especially toward Vinata and her son Garuda—Sesha abandons them and undertakes severe ascetic penance across sacred regions such as Gandhamadana and the Himalaya. His austerities become so intense that Brahma appears and asks his purpose. Sesha declares he wishes to avoid the company of his wicked kin and devote himself to virtue. Pleased by this restraint, Brahma grants him a cosmic duty: to support the unstable Earth. Sesha agrees, descending beneath the world and bearing it upon his head. Thus he becomes Ananta, the eternal serpent whose steadfast virtue literally upholds the world.

highlight_spans.why: The long litany of serpent names emphasizes the vast lineage and mythic scale of the naga race.
Sesha condemns the wickedness and jealousy of his brothers and explains why he withdraws from them.
Brahma invites Sesha to ask for a boon, recognizing his extraordinary self‑restraint and devotion to virtue.
The pivotal command where Brahma assigns Sesha the cosmic task of supporting the unstable Earth.
The concluding image of Sesha (Ananta) beneath the Earth, eternally bearing the world in obedience to Brahma.

top_scenes.scene_text: The emaciated serpent sage Sesha, with matted hair and tattered garments, performing severe penance in the wild mountains as Brahma appears before him in radiant light.
Brahma commanding the colossal serpent Sesha to support the trembling Earth, with mountains, forests, and oceans depicted upon the globe.
The cosmic serpent Ananta deep beneath the world, coiled in the darkness and holding the entire Earth steady upon his immense head.
